title: Come, You Who Are Blessed
story:
A father promised his children that one day he would take them to a beautiful place they had always dreamed of visiting.

The children often talked about the journey. They imagined what they would see, what they would experience, and the joy they would have when they finally arrived.

As the day approached, their father prepared everything carefully. He made sure they had everything they needed and reminded them that the journey would be worth the wait.

When they finally arrived, the children were amazed. The place was even more beautiful than they had imagined.

Their father smiled and said, "I told you that I was preparing this for you."

The children realized that the promise had been prepared long before they understood what it would look like.

In Matthew 25:34, Jesus speaks about the King welcoming those who belong to Him into the kingdom prepared for them from the foundation of the world.

This reminds us that God's salvation is not an afterthought.

God's plan is greater than what we can see today.

There is an eternal future prepared for those who belong to Christ.

Life on earth can sometimes make us focus only on what is happening right now.

We think about our work, family, finances, health, responsibilities, successes, and difficulties.

These things are real and important, but they are not the whole story.

For those who trust in Christ, this life is not the final destination.

There is a kingdom that Jesus has prepared.

The world often measures blessing by possessions, position, comfort, recognition, and success.

Jesus gives us a different perspective.

The greatest blessing is not something we can purchase, achieve, or earn through human effort.

It is belonging to Christ and receiving the inheritance prepared by God.

An inheritance is something received because of a relationship, not something we manufacture for ourselves.

This does not mean our actions are unimportant. Jesus calls His people to live lives of love, mercy, obedience, and service.

Our good works do not buy God's kingdom, but they reveal the reality of a heart that belongs to Christ.

When we understand what God has prepared for us, it changes how we live today.

We can serve without needing applause.

We can give without expecting something in return.

We can forgive even when it is difficult.

We can remain faithful when nobody notices.

We can choose eternal values over temporary rewards.

Sometimes following Christ may feel costly.

You may sacrifice time to help someone.

You may choose honesty when dishonesty would appear easier.

You may forgive someone who hurt you.

You may remain faithful to God when others around you are choosing a different path.

These choices may not always bring immediate rewards.

But God sees them.

And our hope is not ultimately based on what we receive from people in this life.

Our hope is based on the promise of Christ and the eternal kingdom He has prepared.

Imagine hearing the words, "Come, you who are blessed by My Father; take your inheritance."

These are words of welcome, belonging, and fulfillment.

They remind us that God's purpose is not simply to rescue us from something, but also to bring us into something wonderful.

He is preparing us for eternal fellowship with Him.

When life becomes difficult, remember that your present circumstances are not the end of your story.

When you experience disappointment, remember that God's promises are greater than today's losses.

When you feel unnoticed, remember that your Father sees you.

When you are weary from serving, remember that your labor in the Lord is not meaningless.

Keep your eyes on the eternal kingdom.

Live faithfully today because of the hope you have for tomorrow.

The kingdom belongs to those who belong to Christ.

And what God has prepared is greater than anything this world can offer.

Let that promise fill your heart with hope, courage, gratitude, and joy.
life_lesson: God has prepared an eternal inheritance for those who belong to Christ. Do not let temporary struggles or worldly rewards define your life. Live with faith, love, mercy, and service while keeping your heart focused on the eternal kingdom God has promised.
prayer:
Dear Heavenly Father,

Thank You for the eternal kingdom You have prepared for those who belong to Christ.

Thank You for giving me a hope that is greater than anything this world can offer.

Help me remember that my present circumstances are not the end of my story.

When life is difficult, strengthen my faith and help me look beyond what I can see today.

Teach me to live with eternity in my heart.

Help me serve others with love and humility without seeking recognition or reward.

Give me a generous heart that is willing to give, forgive, encourage, and help others.

Help my actions reflect the love of Christ in my daily life.

Keep me from becoming too attached to temporary possessions, achievements, comfort, or recognition.

Remind me that the greatest blessing is belonging to You.

When I feel unnoticed, remind me that You see me.

When I become tired of doing good, remind me that my faithfulness is never wasted in Your sight.

Help me remain faithful even when following You is difficult.

Prepare my heart to live for Your kingdom rather than for the approval of this world.

Thank You for the promise that one day those who belong to Christ will enter the inheritance You have prepared.

May this hope give me courage today and help me live every day in a way that honors You.

In Jesus' name,
Amen.
reflection_question:
Are you allowing temporary struggles or worldly success to become more important than your eternal hope?

How can the promise of God's kingdom change the way you serve and treat others today?

What is one area of your life where you need to live more with eternity in mind?
verse: Then the King will say to those on His right, 'Come, you who are blessed by My Father; take your inheritance, the kingdom prepared for you since the creation of the world.'
